newsitem.title: FRANCE: CCF looks at CIC sale dossier.
newsitem.headline: CCF looks at CIC sale dossier.

text.p: French bank Credit Commercial de France is looking at the CIC bank privatisation file and does not rule out making an offer with other partners, CCF chairman Charles de Croisset said on Thursday.

"We're in the data room but don't read anything more into that. In the data room we are on our own. But at the level of an offer we would unlikely be alone," he told reporters in response to questions.

The French government launched a tender on August 6 for the sale of 67 percent of CIC, which is owned by state-controlled insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) which is itself a candidate for privatisation once CIC is sold off.
The move gave suitors access to confidential data on CIC.
De Croisset told a news conference on the bank's first-half results that it was keen on external growth.
"CCF is very present in the reorganisation of the French banking landscape," de Croisset said.
The bank was "interested in external growth" but its aim was to satisfy shareholders and ensure that growth respected its profitability objectives.
BNP chairman Michel Pebereau declined comment on CIC when asked at a separate news conference on Thursday if his bank was interested.
